mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date coincides with a short-term discount rate compression, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month prior to decision_date
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-increase average (t-test p > 0.05) across 10 such events.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signal deflationary expectations, which reduce risk premia and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months ending on or before decision_date
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-decline average (t-test p > 0.05) across 15 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% suggests a strengthening labor market, which raises corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 1.5% month-over-month while UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the 5-day pre-signal average (t-test p > 0.05) across 10 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior quarter's average, followed by a rebound the next month, indicates a supply shock that initially depresses investor sentiment and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below prior-quarter average and recovers in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 20-day pre-shock average (t-test p > 0.05) across 8 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence catalog; thus omitted) would typically signal strong demand, but here we proxy with HOUST alone. Such a surge predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 days as market anticipates earnings beat.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 3% in the month ending on or before decision_date
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the 5-day pre-surge average (t-test p > 0.05) across 6 such events.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS turns negative, it indicates a sudden drop in credit extension, which raises perceived credit risk and compresses equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of RSAFS turns negative on or before decision_date
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 20-day pre-stress average (t-test p > 0.05) across 7 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a labor market cooling, lowering wage growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.0% for three consecutive months while PAYEMS does not increase by more than 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day pre-cooling average (t-test p > 0.05) across 12 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip industrial production decline (INDPRO) followed by a sustained rise above the prior trough is interpreted as a supply adjustment cycle. The initial dip is associated with negative investor sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days, but the subsequent rebound reverses this effect.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months, then rises above the prior trough in the third month
failure_condition: Across 10 such double-dip episodes, the 20-day forward return in the dip phase is not statistically lower than the 20-day pre-dip average (t-test p > 0.05).
